name: Coup d'Etat
description: Compendium game with six different hands per round: Barbu, Waterloo, Siege, Touche, Guillotine, and Dominos. The Director (dealer) chooses which hand to play; players pay penalties to the Director. The holder of the Coup card may try to overthrow the Director by achieving the hand objective; success makes them Director. Winner is the player with the most money after a number of rounds equal to the number of players.
deck: 32-card stripped (A-7 per suit) plus optional Coup card

history.origins: Believed to have been first played by political prisoners in France over two centuries ago. Published in 1966 by Parker Brothers; the basic game is related to the traditional French game Barbu, with the Coup and Hidden Coup mechanics likely an American addition.
timeline: Late 18th / early 19th century: Game first played by political prisoners in France.
1966: Parker Brothers published the commercial version with Coup and Hidden Coup mechanics.
history.cultural: The game retains French thematic elements (francs as currency, political-prisoner origin story). It was published in the United States and played in home and club settings; the Director's Board and chart-based penalties are part of the commercial edition.
history.evolution: The game developed from an older French game played by political prisoners into the published Parker Brothers version of 1966. The Coup and Hidden Coup overthrow mechanics were added, likely as an American innovation, transforming the basic Barbu-style play into a compendium with a directorship challenge.

setup.players: Two to six players; each plays for himself; partnerships not permitted. For three players, remove sevens and eights from the deck.
setup.deck: Standard 32-card pack (eight cards per suit: Ace, 10, King, Queen, Jack, 9, 8, 7) plus one special Coup card. Suits are Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs; Ace is highest, then 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7.
setup.dealing: Director shuffles and deals eight cards face down to each player and places one card face down in the center. If the center card is the Coup card, Director shuffles and deals again.
setup.equipment: 32-card deck (or standard 52 with agreed stripping), optional Coup card or designated wild card; play money in francs (e.g. 10,000 per player).

rules.objective: Accumulate the most money by the end of the game. Each round has six hands; the Director chooses which hand type to play. In Director play, players pay penalties to the Director for taking forbidden cards or tricks. The Coup card holder may attempt a Coup (or Hidden Coup in Waterloo, Siege, Guillotine) to overthrow the Director and collect from others.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, the Coup card holder announces whether they will try for a Coup. If not, they discard the Coup card and take the center card. The Director then selects one of the six hands (Barbu, Waterloo, Siege, Touche, Guillotine, Dominos) and leads. In trick-taking hands, players must follow suit if possible; highest card in the suit led wins the trick. Penalties are paid to the Director as each hand specifies. In Dominos, play is by sequences (next higher or lower in suit or same rank in another suit); first out of cards wins the hand. A successful Coup pays the attemptor from each player and makes them Director; a failed Coup pays into the Treasury. Rounds equal the number of players; left of original Director starts the next round.
keyRules: Six hands per round: Barbu (avoid King of Hearts), Waterloo (avoid Queens), Siege (avoid Spades), Touche (avoid first and last tricks), Guillotine (avoid all of the above), Dominos (be first out of cards).
Director chooses which hand to play each deal; Coup card holder may try to overthrow or pass.
Must follow suit when able; highest in suit led wins the trick except in Dominos.
Penalties in francs paid to Director; failed Coup pays Treasury; successful Coup collects from each player and becomes Director.

strategy.basic: As Director, avoid taking penalty cards; get rid of high penalty cards early by playing them on others' winners or discarding when you cannot follow suit. As Coup attemptor, choose a hand where your cards give you a realistic chance (e.g. Barbu with several Hearts, Siege with long Spades).
strategy.intermediate: As Director, choose the hand that maximizes your chance to collect penalties given the current deal; avoid leading penalty suits first when rules forbid it. When holding the Coup card, attempt a Coup only when your hand supports the chosen objective (e.g. enough Hearts for Barbu, long Spades for Siege). In Waterloo and Siege, consider whether opponents can block you before committing. Track which hands remain in the round so you do not announce an impossible Coup.
strategy.advanced: Use Hidden Coup in Waterloo, Siege, or Guillotine when you can take all penalty cards without revealing intent; bluff early tricks by appearing upset when taking penalty cards so opponents do not counter you. Balance Treasury risk: failed Coup pays the Treasury, which goes to the next successful Coup or the Director at round end. Manage borrowing (200 francs interest per 1000) and repayment from future winnings. In Guillotine, taking all penalty types is hardest but pays 1500 from each; only attempt with very strong hands. In Dominos Coup, the Coup card is not used; sequence planning and forcing the last card on an opponent are key.
tips: Barbu: Dump the King of Hearts on someone else's Ace or 10, or when you cannot follow suit.
Waterloo: Play Queens on higher cards or discard when not following suit.
Siege: Get rid of high Spades early; small Spades may be acceptable.
Touche: Play low on the first trick; save a low card for the last trick.
Dominos: Hold cards that run in sequence; avoid having only highest or lowest values early.

variations.name: Short Game
variations.description: Eliminate Barbu and Touche entirely. Each round consists of three of the four remaining hands (Waterloo, Siege, Guillotine, Dominos). As soon as three hands have been completed the Directorship passes to the next player. All other rules remain the same.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Short Game only changes which hands are played per round; no engine constant overrides identified yet.

scoring.description: Players pay penalties in francs to the Director for taking forbidden cards or tricks; failed Coup pays the Treasury; successful Coup collects from each player. Settle after each hand and at game end.
scoring.winCondition: Player with the most money after a number of rounds equal to the number of players wins the game.

synthesis.shortDescription: Compendium of six hand types per round; Director selects hand; Coup card holder may try to overthrow; most money wins.
